summary: WS3 adversarial verification of failure-mode classes + untagged-capture harvest from WS1 cold-read logs (Sonnet; Fable in outage)

verdicts.refutation: The three events collectively establish the class, but two distinct stall episodes are conflated into one: e27e964a + 26c8b7e9 document Abyssal's watcher stalling at ~14:07Z on 2026-06-10 (seen-file froze at 3045, dir at 3070, ~16 min blind); 382ed72e documents a separate, later episode the same day where Director Veiled's watcher froze at 15:28:55Z (seen-file stayed frozen while dir grew to 3,164). The class shape treats these as one pattern. They ARE the same root-cause mechanism, but the repeat occurrence within hours on the same day by two different agents on the same CLI is the stronger evidence that this is a systematic tooling defect, not a one-off. That actually strengthens the class rather than weakening it. The mild refutation is: the cure text says "fail-loud per-step deadlines + exit-nonzero; robust polling; self-watchdog" but 26c8b7e9 already demonstrates the viable local workaround (portable polling, fresh ls+diff every 15s) and explicitly notes it cannot silently hang the way the CLI loop does. The cure should be sharpened: the prescribed cure is a rewrite of the watch source to use interval polling as the primary mechanism (not just a fallback alongside fs.watch), since 26c8b7e9 body names fs.watch / FSEvents as the probable failure vector. The current cure text allows keeping fs.watch + adding a reconcile sweep, which is a weaker fix than replacing the primary event source. This is a revision to the cure, not a refutation of the class.
verdicts.correction: The cure should specify interval-polling (readdir + seen-set diff) as the PRIMARY watch mechanism replacing fs.watch, not merely a supplementary reconcile sweep. 26c8b7e9 body explicitly argues this: "prefer interval directory polling … over raw fs.watch on macOS" and Abyssal's own cure was to abandon the CLI entirely and use the portable polling shape. The current provisional cure language ("robust polling") is underspecified and permits a keep-fs.watch-and-add-sweep path that does not fully close the failure mode. Recommend: cure text reads "replace fs.watch primary source with interval polling (readdir + seen-set diff); fail-loud + exit-nonzero on any loop error; stderr liveness heartbeat for external watchdog detection."

verdicts.refutation: The class shape names two mechanisms: (a) per-step deadline killing load-starved drain, and (b) flat-dir growth wedging drain regardless of load. Mechanism (a) is well-evidenced across two sessions and five deaths (4e35c31c, e3f111ec). Mechanism (b) is stated as a closing hypothesis in 4e35c31c ("the comms-dir event count only grows") but is observed in zero events — no death is attributed to corpus size independent of load. A third mechanism not named in the shape is confirmed by 940b435f: an intermittent blocking stall at moderate load (4.5–5.6 load average, no gate chain), host and dir stable, drain wedged ~9 minutes on a 540s budget — the agent attributes this to fs contention or a mid-pass race with concurrent git/registry writes on the .agent tree. The cure ("incremental bounded-batch drain; short budgets; rotation reduces working set") is directionally correct but incomplete: batching does not eliminate a blocking stall if individual batches can wedge on contention; the cure omits instrumentation to locate the blocking call and serialization/back-off on fs contention. The "rotation reduces working set" element cures only the unobserved corpus-growth hypothesis. Additionally, 940b435f's operational inversion — keep budgets SHORT so a wedged drain dies cheap and gap-drain recovers fast — is present in the cure but the reasoning chain (short budget = faster recovery from genuine wedge, not just load-starvation) is not captured in the class body, making the rationale look inconsistent with the load-starvation framing. The class should be regraded to note until an implementer instruments where the drain blocks and the corpus-growth hypothesis is tested independently.
verdicts.correction: Split the class shape into three separately evidenced mechanisms: (1) load-starvation death — well evidenced, cure is batched drain off deadline path; (2) corpus-growth wedge — hypothesis only, needs independent test; (3) intermittent blocking stall (fs contention / mid-pass race) — evidenced by 940b435f, cure requires instrumentation of the blocking call plus serialization or back-off against concurrent .agent writes. Add to the cure: "instrument drain path to locate blocking call; serialize or back-off on .agent fs contention" and drop "rotation reduces working set" as a cure until mechanism (2) is confirmed. Grade as note until all three mechanisms are confirmed and the unified cure is validated.

verdicts.refutation: 6c370ea1 does not support S3 at all. Its subject is skill-invocation-provenance conflated with owner-direction-provenance (ONBOARDING.md was never owner-priority). It carries no heartbeat, no liveness signal, no stale template content, and no retirement event. Assigning it to this class is an error of categorisation; its inclusion weakens the evidence set's coherence. Additionally, 8c6bd26a partially undermines the cure shape: the 20-minute silent gap Misty describes was caused by Monitor primitive/cron degradation on the platform side, not by stale template content. The cure "derive heartbeat args from registry at emit time" is targeted at agents drafting free-form prose that drifts out of date; it does not address a harness-level cron that simply stops firing. These are two distinct mechanisms (content drift vs scheduling failure) that the single cure conflates. 9d421e29 introduces a third variant (blocked-on-owner-ask with a static label) that is also not fully addressed by the provisional cure, which does not mention labelling the blocked state explicitly. The cure shape is partially sound but underdeclares scope: it covers the template-drift vector but needs a separate clause for cron-health monitoring (as Misty names watcher-staleness.ts as the substrate hook) and for labelling the blocked-on-owner-ask state.
verdicts.correction: Remove 6c370ea1 from the cited events; it belongs to a different failure class (provenance-conflation). Revise the cure to name three distinct vectors: (1) template-drift — derive heartbeat body from current claim/cycle state at emit time (addressed by the provisional cure); (2) cron-health — Monitor primitive degradation requires active cron-health monitoring with the watcher-staleness.ts substrate hook (named in 8c6bd26a but absent from the cure); (3) blocked-label — on entering any owner-wait, the heartbeat cycle field must be set to a canonical "blocked-on-owner-ask" label so peers do not interpret the static content as stalled (named in 9d421e29 but absent from the cure). On grade: the pattern is real and recurring (five genuine instances across two sessions), but the cure requires the above three-part revision before it is tight enough to be doctrine. Promote to doctrine only after the cure is revised and the three vectors are explicitly addressed.

verdicts.refutation: The cited event chain has a provenance gap that prevents the class shape from being fully verified first-hand. The original misdirected event (92a73b60) was deleted from the worktree copy before it could be inspected, so the claim that "the proof line printed a relative path that read as the home" rests entirely on the author's self-diagnosis in 9a164c5c and 16939248. There is no surviving artefact proving the write went to the worktree registry rather than simply failing outright. Director Zephyr's contemporaneous diagnosis in eb284f91 frames the failure as the generic silent-write-failure class ("the write's only proof is the proof line; its absence means failure") — not specifically as a relative-path retargeting. The Director did not independently observe a worktree-copy file; the Director observed an absence. Both diagnoses are consistent with what happened, but they are not the same mechanism: a write that silently fails to any path is a different bug from a write that succeeds to the wrong path. The class shape asserts "proof line passes" as distinguishing — but the Director's framing implies no proof line was seen at the Director's read-point either, making the proof-line-passes claim the author's own post-hoc inference about what they saw in their terminal, not a verified observable from the surviving record. The cure's second prong (read the proof line's PATH, not just its presence) is therefore plausible but not confirmed by the evidence: if the write simply failed, the cure is irrelevant; only if the write truly retargeted does the PATH-reading cure address the root cause. The class should remain a note rather than doctrine until a surviving artefact (a worktree-copy file that should not exist) is observed first-hand by an independent verifier.
verdicts.correction: Tighten the class shape to acknowledge the competing diagnosis: the failure mode may be a plain silent write failure (same as the generic class) that the author diagnosed as a relative-path retarget, or it may be genuine retargeting. The distinguishing observable is a file that exists in a worktree comms copy but not in the shared home — no such artefact was preserved. The cure's first prong (absolute paths) is correct regardless of which mechanism applies, because absolute paths prevent both retargeting and the ambiguity that makes post-hoc diagnosis impossible. The second prong (read proof line PATH) is only curative for the retarget variant; it does nothing if the write failed entirely. The cure should be revised to: (1) always use absolute --comms-dir, (2) after any comms write, verify the file exists at the absolute home path by direct stat, not by parsing the proof line. A path-reading check on a relative proof line is insufficient because the proof line text is generated by the CLI at the point of write, not by an independent verifier at the home. Grade stays note: one ambiguous self-reported event with no surviving forensic artefact is below the bar for doctrine.

verdicts.refutation: 40a6ce09 does not strictly fit "malformed argv accepted" — the caller supplied a valid --file flag; the failure was a parser-shape/handler-lookup mismatch (options.files array vs options.file scalar). The argv was well-formed; the dispatch contract was broken internally. The class description conflates two distinct mechanisms under one label. Both fit the structural root cause (no test at the CLI dispatch boundary), but they are not the same failure mode and the class shape should distinguish them.
verdicts.correction: Widen the class shape to cover two sub-patterns: (a) value-validation gap — malformed argument value accepted without type/format check, cascades to an unhelpful downstream error (b797cc73); (b) dispatch-contract gap — parser writes argument to a different key than the handler reads, subcommand wholly broken while sub-boundary tests stay green (40a6ce09). The cure already covers both. Grade should be doctrine: two independent agents, two distinct mechanisms, same structural absence (no dispatch-boundary test/validation), recurrence across sessions spanning weeks.

verdicts.refutation: The watcher self-exclusion fracture in the class shape is not evidenced by either event body. Both events confirm the roster/claim attribution harm but describe the watcher surface only by implication from the general identity-keying doctrine (PDR-027), not from an observed watcher failure. The class shape over-specifies by including watchers as a confirmed fracture point. Additionally, both events are from one session and the retirement event self-tags as behaviour-note; the successor diagnostic task was never completed in the available record, so the root cause (activation logic vs session-local cache/env) remains unresolved. Doctrine grade requires a characterised and validated cure; this evidence supports only that the failure occurred and caused real harm.
verdicts.correction: Cure must add: verify that naming_schema_version records deterministically at schema-activation time, not only a derive-at-use vs cache-at-mint audit. Event 10cb3a10 explicitly flags that fresh post-activation tuples carry naming_schema_version "override" rather than a pinned schema version, indicating the pinning substrate itself may mis-record on the happy path. The cure is incomplete without a confirmed activation-logic diagnostic. Grade should be note until that diagnostic lands and the fix is validated.

verdicts.refutation: No refutation of the class itself. The only adversarial caveat is that the cure's "demo negative case" clause relies on proof that lives in commit 918f022b9 (cited in effea526) rather than being reproducibly specified in the cure text — the cure is asserted sound, not demonstrated inline. This is a completeness gap, not a counter-evidence finding.
verdicts.correction: The class shape names two sub-vectors (pipe tail exit; hook banner mistaken for proof) but e589b3c7 documents a third, distinct vector: under a pipe or background wrapper the push process starts and exits cleanly but the transfer never begins, so even reading the FULL captured output gives a false green because the transfer lines are absent rather than wrong. The cure already addresses this implicitly via ls-remote, but the shape text should name all three vectors explicitly so the class is complete: (1) pipe tail exit not command exit; (2) hook banner is not a transfer proof; (3) transfer simply never starts — absent transfer lines are indistinguishable from suppressed output without an ls-remote verification step.

verdicts.refutation: d8fd08d3 is tagged behaviour-note and its substance about the invisible byte is entirely derivative of 4fd66dc5 (it cross-references it explicitly); it does not stand as an independent supporting instance. The class rests on two genuine instances: 4fd66dc5 (byte already present in source, fooled reviewer and first-hand verifier) and b84fae38 (Write tool materialised escape-intent as raw byte, broke a subsequent Edit). The third cited event is corroborative at best and should not be counted as a primary instance.
verdicts.correction: The class description should note that the two substantive instances are 4fd66dc5 and b84fae38; d8fd08d3 is corroborative only. No change to the cure or grade is warranted. The cure correctly maps post-Write byte-verify to the b84fae38 vector and od -c / RED-first probe to the 4fd66dc5 vector; both clauses are necessary and together cover both attack surfaces.

verdicts.refutation: d9ab3ec7 does not corroborate the silent-drop shape. It documents the inverse: a monitor flood from routing-legacy-fallback diagnostic lines re-emitting every cycle matched by an over-broad grep. Its failure mechanism (too many events rendered, not too few) is distinct from T3. Counting it as a T3 citation overstates the evidence base; T3 rests on a single clean event (6cf5f4ab).
verdicts.correction: Merge both cure components into one statement: (a) test the watcher's exact filter against one event of each shape (directed, untagged narrative, tagged heartbeat, self-authored) before arming — from 6cf5f4ab; and (b) use a narrow channel-token alternation grep and drop 2>&1 — from d9ab3ec7. d9ab3ec7 contributes a valid cure element but should be re-cited as a distinct adjacent class (render flood from diagnostic noise) rather than a second T3 instance.

verdicts.refutation: The shape bundles two sub-claims: (a) format:root at marshal time mangles inline-code content, and (b) it sweeps peer-owned files. Only (a) is confirmed by the cited events. 85bb2336 and 4010748e describe Mistbound's marshal-time format:root mangling an ADR file authored by Misty — a single-file content-damage incident, not a peer-file sweep. The peer-file-sweep clause derives entirely from 89bbb056, which the author (Hushed) explicitly frames as a first-instance graduation candidate requiring a second incident before rule installation. Treating it as confirmed co-equal evidence for T4 overstates the evidential base.
verdicts.correction: Narrow the shape to the confirmed failure: marshal-time format:root damages multi-line inline-code content in peer-authored files, and verify-staged does not catch it because it checks file-list-matches-intent, not content integrity. The cure's second clause ("name peer-owned files before repo-wide auto-fix") should be demoted to a pending-graduation candidate (per 89bbb056's own framing), not promoted into the T4 cure. The primary cure remains: format at author-edit time, verified by the author; marshal must not run format:root as a husky-recovery step; verify-staged must be strengthened to detect content damage, not just file-list correctness.

verdicts.refutation: The three events strongly corroborate the class shape but expose a nuance the shape text does not capture: the Write tool's read-before-write protection is the proximate cause, not simple path reuse. In all three cases (f7a86688 / Lunar, beaba1c4 / Seaworthy, 2c8844ff / Mistbound) the agent issued a Write call to a scratch-path that a prior session had already created, the tool silently refused to overwrite because the file had not been read in that session, and then the Bash comms-append command consumed the unmodified stale file. The failure is therefore a three-party interaction — reused path + Write read-before-write protection + Bash reading the path without verifying freshness — not just path reuse alone. The shape text says "Write read-before-write leaves prior content", which is technically correct, but the operative word "silently" is load-bearing and the shape does not name the tool boundary (Write vs Bash) as the amplifier. All three events also self-diagnose and propose the same cure independently (fresh path or inline --body), which validates the cure direction. One caveat: 2c8844ff carries tag "behaviour-note", not "failure-mode", which slightly weakens its evidentiary weight as a confirmed failure instance versus an observation, though its body is an explicit correction to a polluted prior event.
verdicts.correction: The cure-shape text should be revised to name the three-party mechanism explicitly: (1) reused /tmp path, (2) Write silently no-ops because file was not read in this session, (3) Bash reads the stale file without freshness verification. The cure list is directionally correct but should add: document that Write-to-tmp is unreliable across session boundaries and that Bash cat/append has no freshness guarantee; the structural fix is a session-prefixed path written with Bash (not Write) when the body is non-trivial, or --body inline when the body is short. The note-to-doctrine grade is correct: three independent instances across three different agents in a single session window is enough evidence to graduate to a note entry, but the pattern is a tool-interaction footgun, not a first-principles architectural failure requiring doctrine-level treatment.

verdicts.refutation: 70aed86e does not support this class. Its failure mode is fast-execution on a volatile decision input that the agent read correctly and recently — not reading a stale snapshot as current state. The recency-of-reversal signal it names belongs to a different class (volatile-decision execution risk). Including it in the cure conflates two distinct failure modes. 5cb294ba is adjacent but explicitly self-diagnosed as a compose-vs-emit window variant, not a substrate-snapshot-trust failure: the compose state was accurate at compose-start and the world moved during composition. Only ac9a06af cleanly matches the class shape (frozen in-flight intention surfacing as a remembered completed action, contradicted by authoritative surface reads). One confirmed clean instance with no harm done, plus one adjacent-but-distinct event, does not meet the bar for doctrine. Note grade is appropriate.
verdicts.correction: Remove "recency-of-reversal signal" from the cure — it is sourced from 70aed86e which belongs to a separate failure class (volatile-decision fast-execution). The cure for A2 should cover only: re-derive wall-clock and re-verify each claimed-done external action against its authoritative surface on any resumed turn (sourced from ac9a06af). The 5cb294ba compose-vs-emit axis is a related but distinct sub-variant (temporal dislocation during composition, not on resume) and warrants its own class entry or a clearly-delimited sub-shape. Grade should be note until additional cross-agent harmful instances are observed.

verdicts.refutation:
b46ccedd does not support A3 at all. That event (Airy Lifting Squall, 2026-06-10) records a held-verdict drift caused by reading a live peer worktree mid-flight — the wrong SHA was grounded, not heartbeat-staleness misread as retirement. There is no marshal-cycle, no silence window, no git-vs-heartbeat tension. It is a miscite; removing it leaves only three events for A3.

Of the remaining three: 20eb10fc (Seaworthy) partially undermines the stated cure-shape. Seaworthy DID check git evidence before escalating — HEAD was confirmed unchanged, .git/index.lock absent, no staging window open — and still fired the retirement-detection. In that case git evidence was not suppressed; it was checked and it agreed with the silence signal. The escalation turned out to be a true-positive about session-end (Mistbound had in fact ended), not a false-positive about liveness. Classifying 20eb10fc as a false-positive instance (as the class shape implies) is incorrect: Mistbound was gone, Seaworthy was right. Only 5fb2bcd9 + 670cc290 (Lunar, same session, ~4 minutes apart) are genuine A3 instances, and Lunar explicitly self-reports not checking git before broadcasting 5fb2bcd9.

The cure-shape also needs revision. The provisional cure says "cross-check git log against silence window + direct ping before escalating." 670cc290 names this cure but also names a second discipline: per-landing broadcasts within a marshal-cycle window when silence-since-last-broadcast approaches the 4-min internal threshold. The cure as written places the entire burden on the observer (git cross-check + ping). The marshal-side cure (emit an in-window landing broadcast before the silence crosses the escalation threshold) is equally load-bearing — without it, the observer must know to check git on every sweep, which is a fragile convention. The cure-shape is incomplete without the marshal-side half.
verdicts.correction:
1. Remove b46ccedd from the cited-event set; it belongs to a different class (held-verdict SHA-drift on peer PR review). The A3 evidence set is three events: 20eb10fc, 5fb2bcd9, 670cc290.

2. Revise the event-support characterisation: 20eb10fc is not a false-positive — Seaworthy checked git, git agreed with the silence signal, and Mistbound had genuinely ended. Only 5fb2bcd9 is a clear false-positive instance. The pattern has one confirmed false-positive, not two, across the cited corpus.

3. Expand the cure to two equal halves: (a) observer-side — cross-check git log for commits from the silent agent during the silence window before broadcasting retirement-detection; if new commits exist, treat as work-evidence and substitute a direct ping; (b) marshal-side — within a contiguous-execution window, emit a per-landing broadcast when silence-since-last-broadcast approaches the retirement-detection threshold, even if batch consolidation is the normal discipline. A cure that only covers observer-side discipline remains brittle.

4. Grade as note rather than doctrine. The evidence is one confirmed false-positive in a single session (5fb2bcd9/670cc290), with a self-diagnosis that is accurate but untested as a structural rule. Doctrine grade requires the cure to have been applied and validated across multiple sessions; the corpus only shows the failure and the self-named cure, not the cure in operation. A behaviour-note is the right grade until at least one session demonstrates the git-cross-check + marshal-broadcast cure suppressing the false-positive without introducing a missed true-positive.

verdicts.refutation: No refutation of the class itself — both events confirm it cleanly. The caveat is that the provisional cure is underspecified: "Director verifies chain" is insufficient because the deception vector is a skill name that reads as a team-class authorised action (/team-onboarding). A Director doing a nominal chain-check could still accept a plausible-sounding attribution without a real owner turn to cite. The cure must be strengthened to require the Director to locate and cite a verbatim owner chat turn or owner-direct broadcast — not merely assess whether the joining agent's framing sounds plausible. 280d3f15 surfaces this explicitly: the failure was harder to detect precisely because the skill name implied authorisation.
verdicts.correction: Tighten the Director verification clause: "Director must cite the specific verbatim owner chat turn or owner-direct broadcast — not merely accept the joining agent's attribution as plausible." Skill names that read as team-class actions (e.g. /team-onboarding) are a named deception surface; the positive test is a quotable owner statement, not a plausibility judgement on the framing.

verdicts.refutation: The sole cited instance caused zero downstream harm: the wrong verdict was held (inert, never posted), and discard-and-supersede was frictionless. The event itself notes this explicitly. A class whose only evidence is a contained near-miss with no real review damage is insufficient for doctrine weight. The note grade is correct; promotion to doctrine requires at least one recurrence or a case where the wrong verdict was actually broadcast and acted upon.
verdicts.correction: No correction to cure or shape. The event body independently derives the identical cure (git show <head>:<path>, cite SHA, re-verify at post time), confirming the provisional cure is precisely targeted. The one refinement the event adds beyond the class shape text: the tree need not *change after* reading — a peer's live worktree may already embody their in-flight fix at the moment of reading, which is the sharpest form of the failure and should be reflected in any doctrine wording.

verdicts.refutation: The class rests on a single self-reported event: the authoring agent (Galactic Soaring Nebula, f01540) caught and corrected its own mistake within the same session. No second agent independently observed the phantom signal, and no reviewer corroborates the finding. The description is technically coherent and the slug-dedup mechanism is explicit, but single-source self-attestation means the class has not yet been validated by independent observation. The equal-counts heuristic (methodology counter == finding counter as a stop-and-audit tell) is genuine additive insight from the body that is absent from the cure text — worth folding in if the class is promoted.
verdicts.correction: The cure text should absorb the equal-counts heuristic from the event body: "treat equality between a methodology counter (e.g. dup_slug_records) and a finding counter (e.g. set_changed) as a stop-and-audit signal before investigating further." This sharpens the cure from a general grounding directive into an actionable diagnostic tell.

verdicts.refutation: f693438d (Opalescent Gliding Aurora) is a second Codex agent but its body only states watchers "were not providing attended monitoring" — it does not confirm the specific sub-failure that the watcher ran while failing to wake the agent. It is compatible with the class shape but does not independently verify it. All strong evidence (9bcd58ef and 72204c0c) comes from a single agent instance (Fiery Burning Bellows, session 019ea7) in one session on 2026-06-08, so there is only one independent platform observation, not two.
verdicts.correction: The cure omits a finding from 72204c0c: when a watcher fails to wake, stopping it (rather than continuing to run it) prevents it from emitting misleading liveness signals. The cure should add: "stop the watcher process on platforms where it cannot reliably wake; running a watcher that emits heartbeats without actually waking the agent is worse than no watcher."

verdicts.refutation: No refutation of the class itself — all three events are first-hand and unambiguous. The caveat is on the cure shape: 31998f7a and bd4e39dc show the pre-flight behaviour as a manual peer-to-peer DM convention, not an automated gate at enqueue time. The cure states "commit skill enumerates it" which is directionally correct, but the evidence only confirms a convention has emerged; structural enforcement (skill refuses or warns at enqueue before the commit-msg hook fires) is not demonstrated in these events. The cure should be marked partially implemented / convention-only until an automated check at enqueue is confirmed.
verdicts.correction: Cure shape is sound in direction but overstated in its current form. Revise to: "pre-flight subject length before enqueue — commit skill MUST enumerate the 100-char limit and measure before staging; currently implemented as a manual convention (see 31998f7a, bd4e39dc) but not as a structural automated check. Mark as partially-implemented until the skill enforces character count at enqueue time." bd4e39dc also reveals the structural over-runner pattern: composite subjects of the form `(long descriptor) + secondary + tertiary` reliably exceed 100 chars; the cure should name this pattern explicitly so authors know what to avoid, not just that a limit exists.

verdicts.refutation: Both events come from the same agent (Eclipsed Watching Secret, session 00d760) within 17 minutes, both targeting the same plan file. This is one authoring session discovering two stale cycles in one plan — not two independent incidents across different plans or agents. The evidence base is therefore narrow for full doctrine elevation. The class shape is real but the citation pool is a single plan window, which is appropriate for a note but insufficient to establish the structural failure as cross-plan, cross-agent pattern warranting doctrine.
verdicts.correction: The cure covers 86be55d7 (count-decay: 14 S5443 fixture sites named but zero exist at HEAD) but only partially covers 22dc45ff. In 22dc45ff the dead scope is not a numeric count but a negative-coverage assertion: the cycle assumed eslint.config.ts was not yet in sonar.cpd.exclusions, but the existing glob `**/*.config.*` already subsumed it. The cure should read: "re-ground all cycle scope assertions — counts, named-file site lists, AND negative-coverage assumptions about config/property files — against current HEAD at plan-landing time." Without the negative-coverage clause, a plan author who checks counts but not existing glob subsumption will still produce 22dc45ff-class dead cycles.

verdicts.refutation: The four events are all self-reports or repair-notes from the agents that committed the violation; there is no independent third-party observation. Every event is a "correction acknowledged" or "repair note" rather than a raw proposal-in-flight, so the corpus shows correction responses, not the original deviant proposals. This means the events demonstrate the failure was real and corrected, but they do not show the full shape of a novel violation — they show agents reporting they had already violated and had been redirected. The taxonomy entry is therefore well-evidenced as something that recurs and requires a standing rule, but the cited corpus is entirely retrospective self-report rather than contemporaneous detection. A challenger could argue the doctrine is being derived from the corrected behaviour rather than the driving defect. This is not a reason to reject doctrine-grade — the pattern clearly repeated across at least three distinct agents (Airy, Open, Sylvan/Shaded) and two separate time periods (2026-05-24 and 2026-05-27 through 2026-05-31), which is stronger evidence than a single incident — but any future iteration of this taxonomy should include the original defective proposals (the claim c07f7ab9 scope, the sidecar archives that were deleted) as primary evidence rather than relying solely on correction acknowledgements.
verdicts.correction: None required. The cure (knowledge-preservation-over-fitness; process before archive; fitness is a routing signal) is directly and unambiguously confirmed by all four events. Event 9bb55106 names exactly "never archive unprocessed content" and event c4625cec extends the invariant to buffers explicitly. The two sub-patterns (archive-to-soften-fitness and archive-before-processing) are each attested by at least one event: 53aeb17e covers archive-to-soften-fitness; 9bb55106 and c4625cec cover archive-before-processing; 0b202d8e covers a repair of an archive-only completion claim. Doctrine grade is appropriate given multi-agent, multi-session recurrence.

verdicts.refutation: The class shape is accurate but the provisional cure is underspecified in one critical way: placing the fence "at the reader entry point" assumes a single, stable entry point exists and is enforceable. Event 37523113 shows the contamination path was start-right's required reading order, not an optional or discretionary read of the thread record — the agent followed an institution-level directive that mandated the thread-record read. A fence placed "at reader entry point" that lives in a document that start-right REQUIRES reading does not change the failure mode: the requirement to read it is upstream of any fence inside it. The cure must address the reading-order directive itself (e.g., opener-first dispatch ordering at the start-right practice level, or explicit start-right carve-outs for WS1-class cold-read sessions), not only the physical placement of the fence within a document. Event 8cefbe36 makes the same point: "Your brief's warning landed three minutes after the contaminating read" — the fence arrived too late not because of its location within the file but because the reading order was fixed by a rule above both the file and the fence. The opener-first dispatch proposal in the cure is the sound half; "place fence at reader entry point" is insufficient alone because start-right controls what the entry point is.
verdicts.correction: The cure should be stated as: (1) opener-first dispatch ordering enshrined in the start-right practice itself, with an explicit carve-out: for any WS that requires cold-read blindness, the session opener (not the thread record) is the mandatory first read, and the thread record is deferred or scoped; AND (2) the fence lives in both the opener and a session-open guard in start-right, not only inside the fenced artefact. Physical fence relocation alone is insufficient when the reading order is governed by an upstream rule that mandates the contaminating read. The class shape itself is correct and well-evidenced; the cure as written addresses symptom placement but not root-cause reading-order precedence.
